purpose: Track changes to taxonomy, sources, splits, metrics, inventory, claims, and release governance without retroactive test-driven rule changes.

policy.breaking_change_rule: A change that alters eligibility, labels, IDs, scoring, split membership, or a released interpretation increments the affected contract or protocol version before use.
policy.sealed_test_rule: After test labels or scores are exposed, a rule change cannot be applied retroactively to that evaluation. It starts a new version with a new sealed test or remains a disclosed post hoc analysis.
policy.score_only_rule: A proposal whose only rationale is improving a score is rejected.
policy.append_only_rule: Accepted and rejected records are retained. Corrections add a superseding record rather than rewriting decision history.

records.before: The refined internal roadmap package appeared as an untracked internal/ directory in the public repository working tree.
records.after: The internal/ directory remains local and is excluded as a directory by .gitignore; no internal roadmap artifact is added to the public Git history.
records.rationale: The canonical repository is public and its existing policy already excluded the prior internal roadmap HTML. Keeping the replacement package local preserves that boundary and yields a clean working tree without deleting the files.
records.reevaluation_scope: None for research results; reconsider only if a deliberately redacted public roadmap is later requested.
records.version_change: none; repository visibility changed without altering a research contract or released artifact
records.sealed_test_effect: none; no data, labels, split, metric, or result changed

records.rationale: A single explicit map prevents software checks, dictionary evidence, exposed development results, and downstream associations from silently supporting broader constructs.
records.reevaluation_scope: Future manuscripts, abstracts, releases, and reports must check proposed wording against the map; no completed numerical analysis is reinterpreted.
records.version_change: claim map 1.0.0 created; no executable contract version change
records.sealed_test_effect: none; the map records existing exposure limits and does not alter or reopen a test

records.after: Benchmark metric contract 1.0.0-predata fixes each task's input, numerator/denominator meaning, undefined state, and document bootstrap unit. The standard-library evaluator implements separate open-text point estimates while preserving the legacy supplied-candidate output; probabilistic and selective metrics are conditional and a combined score is forbidden.
records.rationale: Freezing task-specific meanings before source acquisition prevents test-driven denominator changes and keeps gold ambiguity, model abstention, and out-of-inventory decisions distinct. A synthetic executable check is sufficient for the formula gate and makes no performance claim.
records.reevaluation_scope: IR-126 must implement stratified document-cluster intervals, canonical-form sensitivity, and paired comparisons without changing these point-estimate formulas. IR-127 must freeze precision gates before selection, and IR-128 must seal the final metric/version commitment before any test access. Later formula changes require a new evaluation version.

records.before: IR-125 fixed point-estimate formulas and document/canonical-type units, but interval seed, resample count, percentile rule, stratified cluster algorithm, paired-system draw, and degenerate handling were not executable.
records.after: Bootstrap contract 1.0.0-predata fixes 10,000 resamples, a seed, 95% type-7 percentile limits, document resampling within sampling-length strata, global canonical-type sensitivity, identical paired system draws, and the same analysis function for overall and requested frozen strata. Sparse cluster strata and undefined replicates withhold intervals rather than manufacturing precision.
records.rationale: Whole-cluster resampling preserves document and lexical-type dependence while same-draw system differences avoid an unpaired variance assumption. Conservative failure states keep synthetic implementation evidence and future underpowered results from becoming inferential claims.
records.reevaluation_scope: IR-127 must use pilot assumptions with this exact algorithm to freeze allocation and precision gates before selection. IR-128 must commit the metric/bootstrap versions and system order before sealed scoring. Any later seed, resample, estimator, cluster, stratum, weighting, or interval change requires a new evaluation version.

Binding existing IDs to the prior type/source-sense pair prevents source reordering or insertion from silently renumbering citations, annotations, and later releases; explicit failure requires a reviewed lifecycle decision before deletion, split, merge, or supersession.

records.before: The human-readable guide covered target scope and discovery only. Idiomaticity, inventory, contextual sense, uncertainty, the complete executable state set, and the synthetic fixture decision paths remained implicit in the contract or UI.
records.after: Annotation Guide 0.2 supplies a standalone eight-stage decision order with definitions, decision trees, minimum positive, negative, or borderline examples, a complete mapping of every current mwe_contract state, and an explicit M1–M5 synthetic fixture key. A dependency-free test checks state and fixture coverage, while the guide remains stopped before human administration.
records.rationale: A third party cannot reproduce an annotation contract from interface behavior alone. Reusing the current contract states and existing synthetic fixtures closes the documentation gap without inventing new semantics or prematurely writing the detailed hard-case, training, qualification, or adjudication materials assigned to later tasks.
records.reevaluation_scope: Complete IR-141 through IR-146 before freezing a production guide, then test it with authorized independent annotators and retain training, qualification, agreement, adjudication, and revision evidence. IR-115 remains a prerequisite for human administration; document and software coverage alone cannot establish independent applicability or linguistic reliability.
records.version_change: annotation guide advanced from 0.1.0-scope-only to 0.2.0-skeleton and Gate 0 protocol from 1.2.0 to 1.2.1; runtime contract, API, source, inventory, split, metric, and benchmark versions remain unchanged
records.sealed_test_effect: none; the guide re-expresses existing public contracts and project-authored M1–M5 fixtures, adds no source document, natural benchmark item, human label, prediction, score, model, or sealed-test access

records.before: Guide 0.2 named the occurrence, member/gap, and category states but deferred the ordered PARSEME tests, particle movement, inflection, embedded overlap, tokenizer exceptions, and a controlled explanation of exact-span disagreements.
records.after: Guide 0.3 completes the IR-141 occurrence/span/category module without changing the executable contract. It gives ordered terminal-state, member/gap, VPC.full/VPC.semi/VID, embedded-candidate, and frozen-tokenization rules. Twelve project-authored synthetic cases cover continuous and discontinuous realizations, and 13 controlled first-cause codes separate occurrence, span, category, and unclassified disagreements.
records.rationale: Exact-span reliability requires annotators to share both the lexical-member rule and the frozen token boundaries. Applying the PARSEME structural route before its VPC or VID tests avoids using surface familiarity as a category decision, while first-cause coding prevents one member error from being counted again as several downstream gap and category errors.
records.reevaluation_scope: After applicable IR-115 authorization, test these rules in the IR-145 training-only pilot. If category boundaries or exact spans are not applied consistently, stop before production annotation, retain raw disagreements, clarify the responsible rule or narrow scope, version the guide and training cases, and repeat with independent material and annotators.
records.version_change: annotation guide advanced from 0.2.0-skeleton to 0.3.0-occurrence-span-category, IR-141 training cases 1.0.0 were created, and Gate 0 protocol advanced from 1.2.1 to 1.2.2; executable contract, API, source, inventory, split, metric, and benchmark versions remain unchanged
records.sealed_test_effect: none; all 12 cases are project-authored synthetic text, add no Wikipedia or external corpus item, human label, prediction, score, model, or sealed-test access, and cannot be reported as independent annotation evidence

records.before: GitHub Pages was observed publishing the public main branch from the repository root with the legacy build, while internal/ was gitignored but not explicitly excluded at the site-build layer. The visible interface also contained a prototype-stage qualifier, and an obsolete ignored roadmap copy remained at the repository root.
records.after: A root _config.yml excludes internal from the Jekyll site build, a dependency-free check keeps the Pages exclusion aligned with the release manifest and rejects internal paths, internal task identifiers, or the obsolete prototype qualifier in index.html, and the ignored root-level roadmap copy was removed.
records.rationale: Repository visibility and website delivery are different release surfaces. Hiding links and robots metadata do not prevent direct retrieval, so the public site build needs an explicit path exclusion even while the internal working directory remains gitignored.
records.reevaluation_scope: Recheck the delivered artifact whenever the Pages source, build type, branch, source directory, or deployment workflow changes. If Jekyll is disabled or a custom Actions artifact is introduced, enforce the same exclusion in that artifact builder before deployment.
records.version_change: release-layer manifest retains schema 1.0.0 and adds an explicit site-delivery boundary; runtime, API, source, inventory, split, metric, and benchmark versions remain unchanged
records.sealed_test_effect: none; the change controls site delivery and visible wording and does not add or inspect a source document, benchmark item, human label, prediction, or score

records.before: Guide 0.3 exposed the four executable idiomaticity states but did not operationally separate concrete literal, figurative-but-compositional, conventionalized idiomatic, unresolved, candidate origin, or a MAGPIE-style list-conditioned comparison.
records.after: Guide 0.4 defines idiomaticity after occurrence, span, and category and before inventory or sense review. The existing literal state is explicitly compositional/non-idiomatic and records figurative-but-compositional cases with a searchable note prefix; ambiguous and not_assessed remain distinct. Open-text-first-pass and candidate-list-assisted discovery are separated, and a loss-aware MAGPIE projection excludes unresolved and incomparable records instead of forcing a binary label.
records.rationale: Figurativeness alone is not idiomaticity, structural category is not contextual use, and fine-grained sense is a later decision. MAGPIE begins from a fixed idiom list and preserves non-binary outcomes, so a valid comparison must condition on comparable candidate provenance and expose all exclusions.
records.reevaluation_scope: After applicable human-use authorization, test the idiomaticity boundary in the training-only pilot and report multi-state agreement, label distribution, unresolved rate, and the figurative-but-compositional stratum. If the binary projection is unstable, retain the multi-state primary outcome and revise the guide before production annotation.
records.version_change: annotation guide advanced from 0.3.0-occurrence-span-category to 0.4.0-idiomaticity, its synthetic training manifest now points to the current guide, and Gate 0 protocol advanced from 1.2.2 to 1.2.3; executable contract, API, source, inventory, split, metric, and benchmark versions remain unchanged
records.sealed_test_effect: none; the rules use project-authored examples and the published MAGPIE method description, add no MAGPIE row, natural benchmark item, human label, prediction, score, model, or sealed-test access, and cannot be represented as independent reliability evidence

records.before: The executable contract treated every multi-ID decision as ambiguous, had no inventory-ineligible state, coupled out-of-inventory assignment to zero-candidate lookup, and the browser did not let a reviewer record semantic OOI after inspecting matched candidates.
records.after: Guide 0.5, MWE contract 0.11, hybrid inventory contract 2.0, and benchmark metric contract 1.1 distinguish single assignment, jointly applicable senses, unresolved named alternatives, abstention for insufficient evidence, unfinished work, semantic OOI, and inventory ineligibility. The browser exposes the admissible human states after idiomaticity review; validation and evaluation preserve both selected-sense sets and assignment-state accuracy.
records.rationale: A multi-label set does not reveal whether several senses jointly hold or remain unresolved alternatives, while abstention, semantic inventory failure, administrative scope exclusion, and unfinished work answer different questions. Preserving these states prevents forced labels and denominator loss.
records.reevaluation_scope: After applicable human-use authorization, train independent annotators on project senses and measure whether they can distinguish jointly applicable senses, unresolved alternatives, insufficient evidence, semantic OOI, and inventory ineligibility. Revise and version the guide before production if any boundary is not reliable.
records.version_change: annotation guide advanced to 0.5.0-contextual-sense, executable MWE contract to 0.11.0-mwe, hybrid inventory contract to 2.0.0, benchmark metric contract to 1.1.0-predata, and Gate 0 protocol to 1.2.4
records.sealed_test_effect: none; the change uses project-authored state checks and modifies no natural benchmark row, human label, model prediction, score, or sealed-test access

records.before: The guide described several boundary conditions, but no bounded bank guaranteed repeated coverage of pronoun insertion, long gaps, overlap, nesting, coordination, spelling error, punctuation, quotation, and metalinguistic mention with explicit reuse status.
records.after: A ten-case project-authored bank covers every prespecified hard-case stratum at least twice. Each case records admissible decision routes, a rationale, project authorship, redistribution permission, and the absence of third-party text; automated checks enforce the coverage and contract-state boundary.
records.rationale: Synthetic cases expose training and QA failure modes without importing text whose redistribution would need separate permission. Treating routes as admissible states rather than benchmark gold prevents the bank from being misreported as independent annotation evidence.
records.reevaluation_scope: Use the bank only after applicable human-use authorization. If authorized training reveals another recurring boundary, add at least two project-authored or independently cleared cases, version the bank if the decision boundary changes, and repeat the relevant qualification check before production.
records.version_change: hard-case bank 1.0.0 created; annotation guide, executable contract, API, source, inventory, split, metric, and benchmark versions remain unchanged
records.sealed_test_effect: none; all case text is project-authored synthetic training/QA material and no natural source item, human response, prediction, score, or sealed-test information is added

records.before: Synthetic practice and hard cases existed, but instruction, feedback, qualification, task-specific thresholds, exposure control, and retraining were not separated. A public answer key could therefore be mistaken for qualification evidence.
records.after: Training protocol 1.0 stages teach-back, guided practice, feedback, hard-case practice, and independent qualification. Five task gates have separate thresholds and critical sentinels; first failure permits failed-task retraining and one new-form retry, while a second failure stops production work on that task. The actual qualification form remains unmaterialized pending authorization.
records.rationale: Separating learning from assessment prevents feedback-contaminated practice scores and cross-task compensation from qualifying an annotator. A fresh synthetic form per public-repository cohort preserves prospective assessment without importing restricted source text.
records.reevaluation_scope: After applicable human-use authorization, freeze an unexposed synthetic qualification form, administer the staged protocol, and report every task numerator, denominator, critical error, retry, and outcome. Treat the thresholds as provisional and revise/version them before production if the pilot shows ceiling effects, systematic misunderstanding, or inadequate class coverage.
records.version_change: annotator training protocol 1.0.0 created; training-case schema advanced from 1.0.0 to 1.1.0 and Gate 0 protocol to 1.2.5; annotation guide, executable contract, API, source, inventory, split, metric, and benchmark versions remain unchanged
records.sealed_test_effect: none; the protocol and machine-readable gates use only existing project-authored synthetic practice sources and add no qualification form, human response, natural benchmark item, label, prediction, score, or sealed-test access

records.proposer_role: annotation lead / tool administrator / data steward
records.before: The project required mutually hidden independent annotation, discontinuous members, multiple contextual senses, OOI, curation, and audit history but had not assigned these roles between INCEpTION, FLAT, and the browser app or tested a lossless platform-export boundary.
records.after: INCEpTION is provisionally selected for institutionally managed independent first-pass annotation; FLAT remains the fallback and the static app remains an individual review/export instrument. A frozen custom span/link representation and standard-library UIMA CAS JSON converter pass a synthetic format test for gaps, multiple senses, OOI, and audit hashes. No instance, account, or live two-user test has been run.
records.rationale: INCEpTION's documented project roles, workload management, link features, curation, full-fidelity UIMA CAS JSON, and project log cover the required workflow without building accounts or shared storage into the public app. A synthetic format test can safely fix the conversion boundary now, while the institutional decision must govern any real deployment and data storage.
records.reevaluation_scope: After the applicable institutional storage and human-use decision, pin the installed INCEpTION release and configuration, use two annotator-only accounts on synthetic cases, verify mutual invisibility and zero first-pass suggestions, export separate raw UIMA CAS JSON plus the project backup/log, and require the converter and schema checks to pass before any pilot data are admitted.

records.before: The pending ethics record separated held workstreams and listed general questions, but it did not map the exact GSICS preliminary-checklist questions to the proposed annotation route or specify the INCEpTION account, log, export, backup, retention, and release decisions the institution must make.
records.after: The existing ethics record now gives a concrete minimal annotation protocol, full data flow, minimum and excluded person-level fields, a 14-question GSICS working map, platform/security/retention questions, and current LRE ethics and data-sharing requirements. The governance policy also records the current external-platform and retention requirements. Questions 8 and 9, plus question 11 for a paid route, conservatively trigger submission for an institutional decision; no project member issues the decision.
records.rationale: An institutional office can only classify the actual arrangement. Recording the platform and publication facts in the existing evidence file reduces ambiguity without creating a second form or pretending that repository documentation is approval.
records.reevaluation_scope: Before submission to the institutional office, the PI must confirm the applicable unit, recruitment relationship, compensation/funding, session burden, exact host, administrators, automatic log fields, storage, and retention proposal. After a written decision, record its non-sensitive identifier and conditions and revise every affected human-work task before recruitment.
records.version_change: ethics determination record expanded without changing any runtime, annotation, inventory, split, metric, or benchmark version
records.sealed_test_effect: none; this is pre-data governance based on public institutional and journal documents and adds no account, platform deployment, recruitment, human response, source row, label, prediction, score, or sealed-test access

records.before: DEC-2026-09-05-013 conservatively treated annotation-platform accounts, operational logs, and participant-route payment as sufficient reasons to route all independent annotation through an ethics application, leaving IR-115 as a current P0 blocker for unrelated corpus, inventory, and synthetic platform work.
records.after: IR-115 is a conditional pre-human-work gate, not a current P0 blocker. Commissioned or collaborative annotation that studies only the delivered labels is governed first by the chosen work relationship, fair payment, confidentiality, work-product and publication rights, security, and retention. Ethics review applies when people or person-level responses, behaviour, traits, timing, usability, or performance are studied, or when the responsible unit classifies the exact arrangement within its human-research remit. IR-115 no longer blocks independent inventory review or synthetic/platform dry-run preparation.
records.rationale: The governing GSICS materials concern surveys and experiments involving humans. A human-produced annotation artifact, service account, operational log, or payment record does not alone establish that the annotator is the object of research. Keeping the categories separate preserves legitimate safeguards without diverting the current critical path from source rights and target-blind sampling.
records.reevaluation_scope: Before any person is engaged, freeze the worker/contractor/collaborator/participant relationship, payment, rights, account and storage route, and intended analysis. Activate the ethics branch only for human-participant research or when the applicable unit requires it. Intended-user testing and participant-level secondary use remain separate review gates.
records.version_change: governance classification corrected and internal IR-115 status changed from active P0 to conditional P1; no runtime, annotation, inventory, source, split, metric, or benchmark version changed
records.sealed_test_effect: none; the correction changes only governance and task dependencies and adds no person, account, payment, platform deployment, source row, annotation, prediction, score, or sealed-test access

records.before: The internal ledger still showed IR-121 and IR-130 as blocked and ten dependent tasks as queued even though their accepted artifacts and checks were already present in the public repository.
records.after: IR-121 through IR-126 and IR-130 through IR-135 are recorded as done. This is an evidence reconciliation only: it creates no new source, annotation, inventory claim, or human-data claim. The next dependency-ready tasks are IR-136, IR-146, and IR-221.
records.rationale: A canonical work ledger should report completed acceptance evidence rather than recreate finished work or preserve artificial blockers. Reconciliation keeps planning aligned with the existing sampling, split, metric, inventory, audit, and converter artifacts.
records.reevaluation_scope: Reopen a reconciled task only if its cited artifact is withdrawn, its executable check fails, or a versioned contract change invalidates the recorded acceptance evidence.
records.version_change: internal task states reconciled to existing evidence; no runtime, annotation, inventory, source, split, metric, benchmark, or governance contract version changed
records.sealed_test_effect: none; this updates internal planning state only and adds no source row, annotation, prediction, score, person-level record, or sealed-test access

records.before: The transparent STREUSLE occurrence baseline matched only contiguous train lemmas and therefore had zero discontinuous recall.
records.after: The existing hash-verifying STREUSLE checker now also runs a frozen ordered-lemma gap/dependency baseline. Train supplies types and supported dependency relations; the gap and support thresholds are selected from development only. Every optional audit prediction carries rule IDs, evidence token numbers, and the accepted dependency arc. Development discontinuous recall is 8/14 and the dependency filter improves exact-span F1 from 0.316832 to 0.426667 over its lemma-window ablation.
records.rationale: Extending the existing dependency-free checker avoids a second runner and makes the ablation directly comparable. The rule remains deliberately small and explainable; zero unseen-type recall records the remaining candidate-discovery gap instead of hiding it with a model.
records.reevaluation_scope: Apply the frozen rule without tuning to the future project development and sealed-test material after those splits exist. A parser-independent or contextual extension is justified only if the measured unseen-type or discontinuous recall gap remains decision-relevant.
records.version_change: gap/dependency baseline record 1.0.0 created; the STREUSLE benchmark profile remains 0.1.0 and MWE, metric, source, inventory, split, and browser contracts remain unchanged
records.sealed_test_effect: none; STREUSLE test labels and the earlier surface result were already exposed, so the new test diagnostic is explicitly development evidence and no project sealed-test item was accessed

records.before: The candidate inventory required two independent reviews but had no hash-bound review file, complete-coverage validator, or repository-safe separation between public aggregates and restricted work records.
records.after: A public protocol now freezes the 9-form/67-candidate input and structured decisions. One standard-library checker emits a blank template, rejects incomplete, identity-mismatched, non-independent, or non-pseudonymous reviews, and can produce aggregate agreement counts from exactly two completed files. No review has been collected or adjudicated.
records.rationale: A deterministic template prevents scope drift and missing rows while fixed rationale codes avoid unnecessary free text. Keeping completed reviews and identity keys outside the public repository avoids treating human work records as ordinary project artifacts.
records.reevaluation_scope: Reopen the protocol if the candidate inventory hash, source boundary, reviewer roles, collected fields, storage route, or intended analysis changes. Complete IR-136 only after two valid independent reviews and preserved adjudication produce an actual inventory revision count.
records.version_change: independent inventory-review protocol 1.0.0 and checker created; candidate inventory remains 1.0.0-candidate.3 with zero admitted senses
records.sealed_test_effect: none; the review input contains candidate inventory records only and excludes corpus occurrences, development/test labels, baseline predictions, and project sealed-test material

records.before: Protocol 1.0.0 sent all 67 source candidates directly to review using form-level completeness/granularity and candidate-level merge fields, which risked treating source sense count as project or contextual polysemy and implied 387 within-form pair comparisons.
records.after: Protocol 1.1.0 first recomputes a hash-bound polysemy audit. It separates pinned-source coverage, candidate-to-form relation, lexicalized-construction scope, retained-candidate clustering, later contextual assignment, and evaluation. Five gloss-only candidates are flagged mechanically; retained candidates are partitioned into clusters; no contextual claim is available from an inventory containing zero occurrences. The pinned OEWN projection also reconstructs byte-for-byte after replacing one stale generator contract-version constant with the current contract value.
records.rationale: Source identity, usable project granularity, and contextual joint applicability are different constructs. The revised fields preserve those distinctions, reduce unnecessary pairwise burden, and prevent automatic merging from gloss similarity, source order, relations, or model scores.
records.reevaluation_scope: Recompute the audit and reopen the protocol if the candidate inventory, source snapshot, review axes, cluster rule, or contextual-state contract changes. Contextual ambiguity and multiple applicability must be assessed only in a separately frozen occurrence pilot.
records.version_change: independent inventory-review protocol 1.0.0 superseded by 1.1.0; candidate inventory remains 1.0.0-candidate.3 with zero admitted senses, while its artifact hash changes only because the corrected generator hash is recorded
records.sealed_test_effect: none; the audit uses candidate metadata only, no corpus context, annotation, prediction, score, or sealed-test item

records.before: Protocol 1.1.0 placed contextual assignment after lexicographers had already partitioned retained dictionary candidates into proposed project-sense clusters.
records.after: Protocol 1.2.0 places a blinded usage-pair pilot before expert source-to-project mapping. A deterministic standard-library builder extracts all 54 matching STREUSLE train/dev occurrences for the nine frozen forms, excludes test, and creates 51 connected within-form round-1 pairs without bundling source text. Later edges are limited to disagreement or provisional cluster boundaries. Expert review follows the frozen usage-cluster diagnostics; occurrence-to-inventory assignment remains a separate later task.
records.rationale: Primary studies show that semantic granularity, graded or joint applicability, and contextual underspecification cannot be resolved from source sense counts alone. A bounded usage-first stage supplies empirical structure before expert review without adopting a full diachronic DWUG workflow or exhaustively comparing all occurrences or dictionary senses.
records.reevaluation_scope: Rebuild the public manifest and reopen the design if the nine-form inventory, pinned STREUSLE train/dev identities, pairing seed, judgment scale, edge-selection rule, or dictionary-blinding boundary changes.
records.version_change: inventory-review protocol 1.1.0 superseded by 1.2.0; polysemy usage-pilot manifest 1.0.0 created; the candidate inventory remains 1.0.0-candidate.3 with zero admitted senses
records.sealed_test_effect: none; only already exposed STREUSLE train/dev occurrences are indexed, STREUSLE test and the future project sealed test are excluded, no source text is bundled, and no semantic judgment or project sense is created

records.before: The stopped SimpleWiki Route 2 and EXP-2026-09-02-004 retained exposed material for detector/error analysis only. No contextual-contrast successor had been activated.
records.after: IR136-SIMPLEWIKI-CONTRAST-1.0.0 permits developer-only contextual-contrast preparation in the 507 unique verified cached revisions identified by the frozen rendered screen, excluding its one unavailable revision. The complete target list is pick up, come out, make sure. All three search the same cached pool without the old eligibility, sense, centrality, topic or panel filters. The old Route 2 remains stopped; all old records and exposure remain intact. This is not an independent benchmark, an inventory admission, or a human-study approval.
records.rationale: Bounded natural-source contrasts can test whether contextual information missing from the existing development cases is available. Reusing verified, already exposed caches avoids new corpus acquisition and protects the primary target-unexposed English Wikipedia frame.
records.reevaluation_scope: The screen hash e0cce039a3331fffdc0e8ff914506db5004bf7c782d5cceb2d354a5f1cfac148 and deduplicated identity hash 2a914efbd7f9a99174d083ab691e77306a647fb9d3772bfb3e6cf3567236ad0d fix the pool. Preserve verb inflection projection, exact second member, paragraph-local adjacency or 1-8 gaps for the two VPCs, and adjacency only for make sure. Rank compact JSON [IR136-ACQ-0.12, form, page_id, revision_id] by SHA-256, then numeric page/revision; fix the first 20 pages per form and first lead per page. records.after: Both real review commands fail closed while no versioned usage-cluster contract and validator are implemented. In-memory synthetic self-checks remain available.
